elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: New Section 10.6(b) warrants only that services "will conform to the requirements of this Agreement for thirty (30) days following performance"; no professional-and-workmanlike standard appears anywhere in the rendered language (Section 3.8.4's "good scientific manner" is a mutual Development covenant, not a Harpoon warranty).

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Section 10.6(a): "any software delivered to AbbVie under this Agreement will conform to its documentation."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Section 10.6(a) fixes the software conformance period at "ninety (90) days following delivery," not 12 months.
Section 10.6(b) gives services only "thirty (30) days following performance."

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Section 10.6: "AbbVie's remedy ... is repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or re-performance of the non-conforming services."
Section 10.6: "or a refund of the fees paid for such non-conforming software or services."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No Harpoon warranty of compliance with Applicable Law is added; Section 3.8.4 is a mutual forward-looking covenant limited to Development activities ("Each Party shall perform ... in compliance with all Applicable Law"), not a warranty, and Section 10.2 warranties speak only as of the Effective Date.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code warranty appears in Section 10.6 or elsewhere in the rendered text; the drafter expressly declined to pursue it.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Section 10.6(a): "any software delivered to AbbVie under this Agreement will conform to its documentation for ninety (90) days following delivery" — an express software-to-documentation warranty at exactly the 90-day floor.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Section 10.6(b): services "will conform to the requirements of this Agreement for thirty (30) days following performance" — meets the 30-day floor.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Section 10.6 remedy sentence expressly provides "repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or re-performance of the non-conforming services."
Section 10.6 remedy sentence expressly provides "a refund of the fees paid for such non-conforming software or services."

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative text: Section 10.6 supplies a 90-day software conformance-to-documentation warranty, a 30-day services warranty, and both repair/replacement and refund remedies in the same sentence — no element is left to the margin comment.

Preferred level fails on four elements: no professional-and-workmanlike standard, 90 days rather than 12 months for software, 30 days rather than 90 for services, and no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty. To reach preferred the drafter would need to (i) add "the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards", (ii) change "ninety (90) days" in 10.6(a) to twelve (12) months, (iii) change "thirty (30) days" in 10.6(b) to ninety (90) days, and (iv) add express Harpoon warranties of compliance with Applicable Law and that deliverables contain no malicious code.

Minimal: the redline is a single concise insertion of a missing clause, with no edits to Sections 3.8.4, 10.2 or 10.5 and no extras (no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no added procedures or damages categories). Declining to carve the warranty out of Section 10.5 is correct because that disclaimer already opens "EXCEPT FOR THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH HEREIN", so no further edit was needed.

Preserves intent: the new Section 10.6 sits alongside the Effective-Date representations in 10.1/10.2 and the Development covenant in 3.8.4 without contradiction, creates no dangling cross-reference, and leaves the disclaimer, remedies and commercial mechanics of the development and option agreement intact.

Note for the rationale (not a defect): the remedy is stated as AbbVie's remedy without an at-Vendor's-option qualifier, which is marginally more Customer-favourable than the model language and therefore should not be flagged.
